name: Seated knee extension
movement: one knee straightened fully from sitting, held, and lowered

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, leaning on something, two or three metres away, side on to the chair.

words.hint: Sitting on a chair side on, one knee straightened fully and held.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Sit tall on the chair side on to it, feet flat, and straighten one knee.
words.position: Sit tall on a sturdy chair, side on to the phone, back away from the backrest, feet flat, hands resting on the seat.
words.top: One knee locked out fully straight, the thigh still resting on the seat, toes pulled up, trunk tall.
howto: Sit tall on the chair, side on to the phone, back supported or upright, thighs on the seat, feet flat.
Pull the toes up and straighten the knee nearest the phone until it is fully straight.
Hold for five seconds with the thigh still on the seat — the knee, not the hip, does the lifting — and the trunk still, not leaning back.
Lower slowly, over two seconds. The rep counts when the foot is back down. Do a set on one leg, then the other.
words.cannot: The kneecap tracking and the last few degrees of a stiff knee: it sees the knee angle, the thigh on the seat, the trunk and the toes. Lock out as far as the knee allows.
words.about: Seated knee extension (long arc quad) — sitting side on: the knee angle between hip and ankle, at least 165° at the top (fully straight); the thigh staying on the seat, the knee no more than 8° above where it started; the trunk within ±15° of vertical, and not leaning back more than 8° during the lift to help; and the foot's angle at the heel, 60–105°, toes up. The rep is under way once the knee opens past 130° and counts when it is back under 105°. Hold five seconds at the top, lower over two.
words.lost: Sit side on to the camera, whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the knee hurts under the kneecap; straighten less far or hold for less. Keep the movement slow.
words.easier: A shorter hold; straighten as far as is comfortable.
words.harder: An ankle weight; a band around the ankle to the chair leg; a longer hold.
words.mistakes: Not straightening fully; the thigh lifting off the seat; leaning back or slumping to help; swinging the leg up and dropping it.

measurements.label: knee angle

settings.label: Knee angle at the top, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: Sitting it is 90; locked out it is 180. At least 165 at the top. Also the progress measurement.

measurements.label: knee above hip

settings.label: Thigh lifted off the seat, at most (degrees from the start)

measurements.why: The line from the hip to the knee, as its change since the start: + the knee rising — the thigh lifting off the seat to help. Read against the start, so the chair's height does not move it.

measurements.label: trunk off vertical
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off plumb, positive leaning forward: leaning back is the trunk helping the leg up.

measurements.label: trunk still

settings.label: Leaning back during the lift, at most (degrees, negative)

measurements.why: The trunk line, as its change since the start: leaning back (or slumping) to help the knee straighten reads below 0.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee
measurements.why: The foot against the shin, at the heel: it grows as the toes point away. Optional: a foot the model cannot see is not held against anyone.

faults.label: Leaning back
faults.deep: Sit up — the trunk is leaning back to help

faults.label: Leaning back to lift
faults.text: Keep still — let the knee do the work

faults.label: Thigh lifting
faults.text: Keep your thigh on the seat — straighten from the knee
faults.deep: Thigh down — the whole leg is lifting from the hip

faults.label: Not fully straight
faults.deep: All the way — lock the knee out straight
